provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Hollowing solid rectangles is invariant under every D4 transform: a rectangle's bounding box maps to a rectangle's bounding box. Its 1-cell frame maps to a 1-cell frame and its interior maps to an interior. So no direction or axis needs specializing. The only role is the background colour. The factory fixes it as the constant palette[0] rather than inferring it as the most common colour. The generator can produce grids where one box's area is larger than the background area, for example an 8x10 grid with an 8x6 box, so a most-common-colour guess could fail there. The emitted program works in visible coordinates. It finds 4-connected single-colour components of non-background cells. The generator keeps a 1-cell margin between boxes, so each component is one rectangle. For each component whose bounding box is at least 3 cells in both dimensions, it sets the strict interior of that box to background. Boxes touching the grid edge are handled naturally.
draft_notes.limitations: Assumes the generator's domain: background is the original colour 0, and the rectangles are solid, single-coloured and separated by at least one background cell. Two touching same-colour boxes would merge into one component, and the generator rules that out. Components with 2 or fewer rows or columns stay unchanged, matching the archived solver; the generator itself always uses sizes of at least 3. The fixtures agree with the uniform rule, and none contradict it.
